cards.back: Family sharing a general formula and functional group; successive members differ by CH₂; boiling points rise gradually along it.
–OH alcohol · –X halogenoalkane · C=C alkene · –CHO aldehyde · C(=O) in-chain ketone · –COOH carboxylic acid · –COO– ester · –NH₂ amine · benzene ring arene.
Longest chain → lowest locants → functional group suffix priority. Number from the end that gives the lowest numbers.
Same molecular formula, different atom arrangement (C₄H₁₀: butane + 2-methylpropane). Branching lowers boiling point (weaker London contact).
Bromine water: decolorizes rapidly with C=C (addition), stays orange with alkanes. Quick unsaturation test.
Primary (C–OH carbon bonded to 1 C), secondary (2 C), tertiary (3 C). Class decides oxidation products.
Primary → aldehyde (distil as formed) → carboxylic acid (reflux, excess oxidant). Secondary → ketone only. Tertiary → resist mild oxidation.
Aqueous NaOH → substitution → alcohol. Ethanolic NaOH, heat → elimination → alkene. Same reagent, solvent decides.
C=C opens: H₂/Ni → alkane · Br₂ → dibromo · HBr → halogenoalkane · H₂O/catalyst → alcohol (Markovnikov: OH to the carbon with fewer H).
Alkene C=C bonds open and link: ethene → poly(ethene). Polymer has the same empirical formula as the monomer; saturated chain.
Carboxylic acid + alcohol ⇌ ester + water, warm with acid catalyst. Condensation reaction — esters are fruity-smelling.
Alkane + Cl₂ needs UV light: initiation (Cl· formed) → propagation chain → termination (radicals pair). Homolytic fission.
Delocalized π ring, equal C–C bond lengths (order 1.5) → reacts by SUBSTITUTION, not addition — the ring's stability is preserved.
Broad 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ = O–H (alcohol/acid) · sharp ~1700 cm⁻¹ = C=O · ~1700+ broad = carboxylic acid. Functional groups, not full structure.
Butanone — secondary alcohol → ketone, and ketones resist further oxidation. (Butan-1-ol would give butanal then butanoic acid.)

cards.front: Distil vs reflux when oxidizing a primary alcohol?
cards.back: Distil immediately → aldehyde escapes before oxidizing further. Reflux with excess oxidant → goes all the way to the carboxylic acid.
Limited O₂ → CO (toxic) + soot (C) instead of CO₂. Complete combustion: full oxidation to CO₂ + H₂O.

cards.front: Command term: State the reagents and conditions
cards.back: Both required: reagent (e.g. acidified K₂Cr₂O₇) AND condition (reflux/distil/heat). Naming the organic product at each step is expected too.
Work backwards: target functional group ← reaction that makes it ← starting alkene/halogenoalkane. E.g. propene → hydration → propan-2-ol → oxidation → propanone.
